parts.name: Thyroid cartilage
parts.attachment_or_location: two laminae meeting anteriorly at the laryngeal prominence; superior and inferior horns
parts.function_note: The largest laryngeal cartilage and the Adam's apple. Hyaline, so it ossifies with age and becomes visible on plain films. Its inferior horn articulates with the cricoid at the cricothyroid joint, the axis about which cricothyroid tilts the cartilage to tense the vocal folds.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

parts.name: Cricoid cartilage
parts.attachment_or_location: complete signet-shaped ring: narrow anterior arch, broad posterior lamina
parts.function_note: The ONLY complete cartilaginous ring in the airway, which is why cricoid pressure can occlude the oesophagus behind it, and why a cuffed tube is avoided in small children whose cricoid is the narrowest point of the airway.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

parts.name: Arytenoid cartilages (paired)
parts.attachment_or_location: pyramidal, sitting on the upper border of the cricoid lamina; vocal process anteriorly, muscular process laterally
parts.function_note: Every intrinsic laryngeal muscle except cricothyroid moves these. The vocal ligament attaches to the vocal process and the muscles to the muscular process, so rotating the arytenoid abducts or adducts the fold.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

parts.name: Epiglottic cartilage
parts.attachment_or_location: leaf-shaped elastic plate attached by its stalk to the back of the thyroid cartilage
parts.function_note: Elastic rather than hyaline, so it never ossifies. It is displaced passively by the tongue base and by laryngeal elevation rather than actively folding down.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

parts.name: Corniculate and cuneiform cartilages
parts.attachment_or_location: small nodules in the aryepiglottic folds, above the arytenoid apices
parts.function_note: Stiffen the aryepiglottic folds; visible as paired bumps at laryngoscopy and useful landmarks for identifying the glottis.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

function: Form the skeleton of the larynx: a rigid framework that keeps the airway open, carries the vocal folds, and provides the levers the intrinsic muscles act on to control pitch and glottic aperture. The laryngeal muscles in data/muscles/ attach here; because these are cartilage rather than bone, those muscles record their attachment against the adjacent hyoid in the skeletal frame.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

parts.name: Tracheal cartilages (16-20 C-shaped rings)
parts.attachment_or_location: incomplete rings, deficient posteriorly where the trachealis muscle closes the gap
parts.function_note: The posterior gap lets the oesophagus expand into the trachea during swallowing, and lets trachealis narrow the lumen to raise expiratory air velocity during a cough.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

parts.name: Carina
parts.attachment_or_location: keel-shaped last tracheal cartilage at the bifurcation
parts.function_note: The most sensitive site for the cough reflex, and the landmark for tube position. The right main bronchus is wider and more vertical, which is why aspirated material goes right.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

parts.name: Bronchial cartilage plates
parts.attachment_or_location: irregular plates replacing rings as the bronchi divide, disappearing at bronchiolar level
parts.function_note: Their disappearance defines the bronchiole, and is why bronchioles collapse in expiration when the surrounding lung loses elastic recoil.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

function: Hold the conducting airway open against the negative intrathoracic pressure of inspiration while remaining flexible enough to allow neck movement and swallowing.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
